column3: BSB supplies “Jesus” and renders the Greek present verbs as past narrative.
“Here” is supplied after “bring it.”
BSB’s “will return it” follows the critical text with “back” (πάλιν), which the Textus Receptus lacks.
“Untied” renders the Greek present “untie.”
BSB recasts “What are you doing, untying the colt?” as a question about why.
“The disciples” and “the people” make the Greek pronouns explicit; the Greek says Jesus “said,” rather than “instructed.”
BSB renders the Greek present verbs “bring” and “throw” as past narrative.
“In the crowd” is supplied; spreading the branches is implicit in the Greek elliptical clause.

BSB’s “Jesus” matches the Textus Receptus (Ἰησοῦς); BSB renders the present “come” as past and names buyers before sellers.
“Merchandise” specifies the more general Greek word for a vessel or implement; “courts” is supplied.
“Began” is supplied; the Greek says He was teaching and saying.
